correctness.rationale: The two-node block symbol follows directly from evaluating the three Lagrange basis functions at r and 1+r. Its squared singular values have the stated trace and squared determinant, both affine in z=(1-Re q)/2. For u>0, X(u) is at least one and lies to the right of the vertex F(z)/2; the characteristic polynomial evaluated at X(u) is strictly positive for z>0 since X(u)<(2+u)/(2(1-u)). This strictly excludes all other Fourier blocks for noninteger displacement. The derivative of X is positive, and the half-step zero block takes (1,3) to (5/2,5/2); an exact independent N=2 construction reproduced the 5/4 squared ratio and the block maximum. Translations by two nodes and reflection reduce any real shift to r in [0,1] without changing the norm or u; integer shifts are permutations. The result is in the unweighted coefficient norm, and the finite reproduction does not replace the all-mesh proof.
